intro: Decemberists members with a bluegrass and tango string band.
story: Black Prairie began in 2007 as a Portland string band of Decemberists Chris Funk, Nate Query and Jenny Conlee with Annalisa Tornfelt and Jon Neufeld, blending bluegrass and tango. Feast of the Hunters' Moon, produced by Tucker Martine for Sugar Hill, came out in April 2010, the year they played Pickathon, and American Songwriter gave it four stars. A Tear in the Eye Is a Wound in the Heart followed in 2012 and Fortune, a turn to garage folk-rock, in 2014, and the group went on hiatus around 2018.
artist_reel_line: The group went on hiatus around 2018 as members took up other projects.

intro: Ragged, literary Americana from New Jersey.
story: Roadside Graves, a Metuchen, New Jersey folk-rock band founded in 2000, brought ragged, literary Americana to Pickathon in 2010. We Can Take Care of Ourselves, based on the S.E. Hinton novel, followed on Autumn Tone in 2011, then Acne / Ears in 2015 and That's Why We're Running Away in 2020. I Won't Cry Alone, their seventh full-length, came out on Don Giovanni in October 2023, and frontman John Gleason still gathers the band's community in Metuchen for events like the Family Pizza Show.
artist_reel_line: John Gleason hosts the Family Pizza Show in Metuchen.

story: Weinland is the Portland band of Adam Shearer, a Kalispell, Montana native who moved to Portland in 1998, and its somber, sweeping folk-rock reached Pickathon in 2010 with Breaks in the Sun, on Badman, behind it. Willamette Week called that 2009 album heartbreakingly gorgeous. Los Processaur followed in 2012. Shearer also sings with Alialujah Choir, and Weinland has been quiet on record and on the road in recent years.
artist_reel_line: Frontman Adam Shearer went on to form Alialujah Choir.

intro: A street-singing ragtime and country-blues troubadour.
story: Woody Pines, an Asheville-rooted ragtime and country-blues troubadour who sang on streets across the country, came to Pickathon in 2010, his second visit, with Counting Alligators behind him, an album co-produced by Gill Landry with Ketch Secor among the guests. A self-titled album followed on Muddy Roots Music in December 2015. He later settled in Nashville and kept touring roots venues.
artist_reel_line: He later settled in Nashville and kept touring roots venues.

story: Seth Bernard and May Erlewine, who met at the 2003 Ann Arbor Folk Festival and co-founded Michigan's Earthwork Music collective, brought community-minded folk to Pickathon in 2010, billed as Daisy May and Seth Bernard. Their first joint album came in 2006 and Welcome Back in 2009, and a 2012 album was inspired by a journey across Ethiopia. Erlewine's seventh solo album, Where We Are, came out on Earthwork in 2014, and she released new albums in 2025 and 2026.
artist_reel_line: May Erlewine released new albums in 2025 and 2026.

intro: A vintage jump-jazz trio from Seattle.
story: Casey MacGill brought vintage jump jazz with his Blue 4 Trio to Pickathon in 2010, one of three visits, with MacGill on piano, cornet and tenor ukulele. The Seattle trio held a weekly gig at Tutta Bella, made three CDs, the latest called Barrelhouse, and toured European swing-dance festivals. The full combo is less active now, but MacGill still plays regular local club sets for Seattle audiences in 2026.
artist_reel_line: MacGill still plays regular local club sets in Seattle in 2026.

intro: A former Everybodyfields bassist turned songwriter.
story: Sam Quinn co-founded the everybodyfields with Jill Andrews, whom he met in 1999 when they were counselors at a Tennessee summer camp. The band disbanded in June 2009 so each could go solo, and Quinn brought candid, conversational songwriting to Pickathon in 2010. The everybodyfields reunited for Bristol Rhythm & Roots in September 2011. Based in East Tennessee, he performs regionally with his band The Cartwright Brothers and returned to Down Home in Johnson City in November 2026.
artist_reel_line: He played Down Home in Johnson City in November 2026.

intro: A Vermont songwriter with a new folk opera.
story: Anaïs Mitchell played Pickathon in 2010 with Hadestown, a folk opera on record, newly released. The project became a Broadway musical that won the 2019 Tony Award for Best Musical, with a Tony for her score, and in 2020 its cast album won the Grammy for Best Musical Theater Album. Her song "Bright Star" earned a solo Grammy nomination in 2023, and a film of the stage show reached North American theaters in July 2026.
artist_reel_line: Her score for Hadestown won the 2019 Tony Award for Best Original Score.

intro: A songwriter with a long Drag City catalog.
story: Bonnie "Prince" Billy is the name Will Oldham has recorded under since 1999, after Palace Brothers and Palace Music, and he played Pickathon in 2010 with The Cairo Gang. Best Troubador came out on Drag City in 2017 and I Made a Place in 2019, then Blind Date Party, with Bill Callahan, in 2022. Keeping Secrets Will Destroy You, his 21st studio album, was recorded at home in Louisville in 2023. He came back in 2024, and The Purple Bird followed in 2025 and We Are Together Again in 2026.
artist_reel_line: The Purple Bird came out in 2025, and We Are Together Again in 2026.

story: Typhoon, formed in 2005 by Kyle Morton, Toby Tanabe and Dave Hall, high-school friends from Salem, Oregon, grew into a Portland collective of orchestral indie rock. Hunger and Thirst, their first full-length on Tender Loving Empire, came out in 2010, the year they played Pickathon, and they made their Late Show with David Letterman debut in 2011. White Lighter followed on Roll Call in 2013 and Offerings in 2018. They played two concerts in January 2026 for their 20th anniversary and came home in September 2026 for an outdoor set on Sauvie Island.
artist_reel_line: They played an outdoor set on Sauvie Island in September 2026.

intro: A Bay Area troubadour blending folk and soul.
story: Sean Hayes, born in New York City, raised in North Carolina and long based in San Francisco, was an under-the-radar troubadour blending folk and soul when he played Pickathon in 2010, his second visit. NPR profiled his self-released albums, among them Flowering Spade, and Be Like Water followed. After moving to Sonoma County he made his ninth full-length, his first in five years, in 2021, and he released his tenth album, Bright on Bright, in 2026.
artist_reel_line: Bright on Bright, his tenth album, came out in 2026.
